findings.title: verify-act.js's `mode: 'batches'` branch is dead code — no caller ever sets it
locations: instruments/check-consistency/workflow/verify-act.js:99-121 (the whole `if (MODE === 'batches') {...}` block, including its own coverage-gap validation of a `batches` array)

src/CLI/Passes.jl:542 (`act = merge(base, Dict("range" => fixrange, "mode" => "lanes", ...`) — the ONLY call site in the codebase that builds args for verify-act.js, and it always hard-codes `"mode" => "lanes"`, never `batches`
findings.contradicts: the file's own header comment: '... mode ∈ lanes|batches from args ...' (verify-act.js:6), which states both modes are live
findings.description: verify-act.js declares and carefully validates a second operating mode (`mode: 'batches'`, with its own gap/overlap/duplicate-coverage checks over an `A.batches` array of [from,to] ranges), but grepping the whole Julia source and test suite shows exactly one call site ever constructs this script's args (Passes.jl:542), and it always passes `mode: 'lanes'` and never supplies a `batches` array; no test in test/rounds.jl, test/coverage.jl or test/schemas.jl exercises `mode: 'batches'` either. The batches branch, including its coverage-gap detection, is unreachable in the shipped tool: a bug there would never be caught by anything that runs, and the header comment tells a reader a capability exists that the CLI never uses.
findings.resolution_hint: Either wire a real caller for `mode: 'batches'` and cover it in test/rounds.jl, or delete the batches branch and the `mode` arg entirely and correct the header comment — an instrument script the design says is frozen per-commit should not carry a path only a hand-run Workflow call could ever reach.

findings.title: Inconsistent 'refuse on an empty item list' guard across the eleven scripts
locations: instruments/check-consistency/workflow/verify-act.js (no such guard in the default `mode: 'lanes'` path)
findings.description: Four of the eleven scripts explicitly refuse to run when their driving item list is empty, each echoing RULE.TEST.MISSING_IS_FAILING ('a zero count is a dead lane rather than a clean one'). The other seven — including the three main per-instrument entry points lanes.js, panel.js, hunt.js and audit.js — have no equivalent guard on their own `A.lanes`/`A.hats` array: invoked with an empty roster, each would iterate zero times and return a quiet `{written: [], dead: [], empty: [], truncated: []}`, indistinguishable from 'nothing to check' rather than a loud failure. Under the current CLI (Preflight's lane/hat resolution) this looks unreachable in practice, so it is reported as a design-consistency gap, not a demonstrated failure.
findings.resolution_hint: Add the same `if (!A.lanes.length) throw ...` (or `.hats.length`) guard to lanes.js, panel.js, hunt.js, audit.js, verify-state.js and the `lanes` branch of verify-act.js, matching the wording already used in dismissals.js/severity-recheck.js/rubric-audit.js/verify-architecture.js.
